#2013. Rio Ferdinand disappointed Man Utd didn’t sign midfielder better than Elliot Anderson

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

“He came on and showed PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France,” Ferdinand said.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

Rio Ferdinand suggested Bouaddi’s quality could soon make the midfield position in a packed Manchester City his regular role.

City already have Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among their midfield options, but Ferdinand believes Bouaddi has the ability to stand out alongside them.

“They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily.”

#2012. Manu Koné: Roma slap £86m price tag on Chelsea target

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

“There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”

D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I said it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of important players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

Koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

For now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

#2011. £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA

Might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

At least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match plan at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO

2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7

2 - Tottenham Hotspur have lost their opening two matches of a league campaign without scoring for the first time since the 1974-75 season.Concerning. pic.twitter.com/N8izpVYslx

Jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl

Barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle showed little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

The visitors are in dreamland! Hall swings in a corner and Woltemade towers above Udogie to win the header. The ball breaks to Wissa, who fires a delightful acrobatic finish into the net, extending Newcastle’s advantage. Spurs’ crisis deepens. They’re on course for two defeats to start the season.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. The full-back cushions a header into Elanga, who swivels and slides a low effort in off the post to open the scoring and send the away support into a euphoric sea of celebration. What answers do Spurs and De Zerbi have now?

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

Newcastle deserved that goal. They have been the stronger side since the halftime interval, and this is the Anthony Elanga that Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer.

He scored on the opening weekend against Liverpool, but this was an even better finish, spinning sharply and sweeping a shot home on the turn. Smart dance moves for the celebration too.

It all came about from another long diagonal ball forward, but this time it was inch perfect from Nico Gonzalez for Harvey Barnes to put a header into the path of Elanga inside the box.

Newcastle are really growing into this contest, with Spurs getting deeper and deeper. Elanga is starting to get some joy out wide.

The momentum has arguably been with Newcastle since the interval. They’re pushing Spurs back towards their own goal. The visitors are waiting to fashion a real big chance.

Elanga latches onto Hall’s pass, gets in behind Spurs’ defence and beats Kinsky to the ball. However, it was a difficult pass to control and his touch is too heavy, causing the opportunity to disappear. Newcastle are certainly looking more adventurous at the start of this second half.

The visitors make a rare foray forward as Hall bends an ambitious curler from long range that flies off target. That is more encouraging for Newcastle.

Early drama at the start of this half as Spurs appeal for a penalty. Thiaw and Marmoush challenge for a 50-50. The Tottenham forward crashes to the floor as the Newcastle captain goes for the clearance. The referee’s on-field decision is no penalty and VAR agrees. After seeing the replays, there wasn’t too much contact and it would have been a harsh penalty if given.

We are back under way for the second half. Will we see a goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this evening?

Spurs have been knocking on the door and looked like the far more threatening side, but they’ve been unable to find an opening goal. Newcastle have defended diligently and frustrated their opponents. However, in forward areas, they look disjointed and are lacking serious firepower.

⏸️ @SpursOfficial 0-0 @NUFC There's nothing to separate the two sides at half-time pic.twitter.com/ICFqQ3eXMO

Tel has drifted out to the right wing and turns inside of Nico before whipping a ball into the box which narrowly evades Marmoush. Tonali then bursts forward and passes to Porro, but Hall thwarts Spurs’ latest attack by blocking the makeshift winger’s shot.

I would be worried if I were Matthias Jaissle. Newcastle have not looked comfortable dealing with Tottenham’s corners and goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek has made a couple of good saves this half to keep the scores level.

Much of Newcastle’s attacking play has been aimless, with long diagonal balls pumped forward that the Tottenham defence is prepared for and has tended to deal with easily.

Very little is happening in midfield and neither Joe Willock in the number 10 role nor Yoane Wissa at centre forward has had any real joy in the final third.

It all looks a bit predictable going forward and, if we are being ultra critical, a bit aimless too. They have not forced a save from the Spurs goalkeeper as we approach half time.

Marmoush has become far more involved over the last ten minutes and has showcased his quality with a few notable touches and darting runs. Nevertheless, Spurs have been unable to breach Newcastle’s stubborn defence.

A free-flowing Tottenham move involving Van Hecke and Marmoush ends with Porro sliding a low cross in towards the unmarked Tel at the back post. The Spaniard doesn’t quite can’t enough power on the delivery and Hornicek rushes out to collect.

Marmoush slips a clever pass through to Robertson, who fires in a first-time cross which flies out for a corner. Fernandes whips a corner into the box and Van Hecke wins the header, beating two Newcastle players to the ball. But Hornicek is there to parry the Dutchman’s close-range header away.

Robertson’s deep corner finds an unmarked Marmoush at the back stick. He takes a first-time shot, but his volley bounces wide of the near post. From that range, he needs to be getting that on target.

Marmoush has been on the periphery so far today. Spurs have looked threatening but they could be more attentive with possession at times, especially in midfield.

Van de Ven makes a crucial challenge to stop Wissa from fashioning a shooting opportunity inside the six-yard box after good build-up play from Nico and Elanga.

Newcastle are trying to get the ball forward quickly in this new “vertical” style of Matthias Jaissle but all it is doing at the moment is give it straight back to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has not been a fun first 20 minutes to watch from the visitors who have had little joy breaking through the lines and have invited pressure from Spurs.

The less said about their set piece delivery the better. Harvey Barnes has taken over corner duties from Bruno Guimaraes and has not managed to clear the first Tottenham defender yet.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

Tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are currently in the ascendency.

Tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

Tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very new-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

Newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

We are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

With just under ten minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two line-ups this evening.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Roberto De Zerbi has explained Sávio's absence from our matchday squad ℹ️📲 https://t.co/ACZscgieFg pic.twitter.com/ddGz2NveX3

“It was bad news yesterday before training in the afternoon because he suffered muscle fatigue and the medical staff obviously didn’t want to take a risk and I agree with them - it’s not the right moment, especially because he didn’t work in the last 10 days, for him 20 minutes against Charlton, maybe it was tough to rest for the days after but for the next game I think there are no problems.”

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm

"If I'm a Tottenham fan, this is the most excited I've been in MANY YEARS"Jamie Redknapp thinks that Spurs have built a strong squad that can compete in the Premier League 👀 pic.twitter.com/55Dwm7BaoE

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Nico will make his NUFC debut today 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ilEM8w3Dwd

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”

Tottenham had been hoping to see Savinho following his glittering cameo which yielded a goal and an assist against Charlton on Wednesday, but they will have to wait for his Premier League debut.

Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

Nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

#2010. Anis Mehmeti's Ipswich Town situation hasn't changed - Derby County, Birmingham City will watch

As the calendar year comes to an end, murmurs are starting to swirl around which fringe Premier League players may find themselves in the Championship during the January transfer window, and Ipswich Town's Anis Mehmeti has to be one of them.

The Albanian international was on the move last January, signing for the Tractor Boys midway through the campaign for a reported fee of just £3 million, with his contract at Bristol City in its final six months.

Mehmeti had established himself over the past 18 months at Ashton Gate as a top Championship attacking midfielder and someone on the fringes of making that jump to the Premier League, and he did so at Portman Road.

The 25-year-old's top-flight dreams have been quite nighmareish so far this season, though. He's yet to make a league squad for Gary O'Neil's side, who have enjoyed a decent start to life back in the Premier League without him.

As January approaches, he'll surely be someone touted for a short-term move to get some more game time, and a few of the sides who had interest in him this past summer should be retaining that.

Discussion surrounding whether Mehmeti would be able to make the step-up to the top flight with Ipswich was swirling back in the summer. With the 25-year-old not in Gary O'Neil's plans in the first month of the season, many were expecting him to leave by deadline day.

Derby County were interested, as were Hollywood duo Wrexham and Birmingham City, but the 25-year-old declined the option to move back to the Championship, instead choosing to fight for his place at Portman Road.

Mehmeti has appeared in just one game in all competitions for the Tractor Boys this season: their 4-2 defeat in the EFL Cup against Arsenal. He did score in that game, but the performance evidently wasn't enough to warrant even a place on the bench in a Premier League outing.

Two and a half months on from deciding to stay at Ipswich, that doesn't seem to have been the right choice. With the transfer window opening soon, he may find himself tempted to prove himself once more in the league below.

Both Derby and Birmingham have experienced a stark contrast in their starts to the Championship campaign.

Chris Davies' side sit atop the second tier at the November international break, while John Eustace was close to the sack before a relieving 3-1 win over Bolton Wanderers in the final game before the break - just their second victory this season, and their first at Pride Park.

The Rams are still inside the bottom three, but have some newfound belief that the campaign can be salvaged in the coming months, especially with the good news surrounding some starters returning from long-term absences, which have contributed to this poor start.

Despite being at opposite ends of the table, though, both sides could use someone like Mehmeti on their side for the second half of the campaign.

Where do you think Anis Mehmeti will be playing come the end of the January transfer window? Let us know in the comments.

We saw last season that the 25-year-old is comfortable coming into a side already challenging for promotion and settling in quite quickly. Mehmeti started 12 of the 19 games he was available for in Kieran McKenna's side last year, scoring and assisting twice.

Meanwhile, Derby need goals. The three against Bolton was just the third time this season they'd scored more than once in a game, and the first time since their last win at Portsmouth on September 1st. Mehmeti can provide that from an attacking midfield position.

John Eustace knows how to get the best out of a goalscoring attacking midfielder, as seen with Sammie Szmodics in the 2023/24 Championship campaign.

Even now at Derby, the Irishman has been the Rams' most dangerous goal threat this season, with four goals in 14 games before undergoing knee surgery earlier this month, which will see him out for around five more weeks.

With Mehmeti as a versatile option across the three behind a striker, bringing him in won't force Szmodics to watch on from the sidelines. They could easily both play together, and those two behind a returning Patrick Agyemeng could transform this Derby frontline in the new year.

The Albanian international netted 12 for Liam Manning's Bristol City side en route to the play-offs a couple of years ago, before starting last season with nine goals and six assists in all competitions at Ashton Gate ahead of his move to Ipswich.

If he can contribute with nearly as many goal contributions in the second half of this season, Derby won't need to worry about relegation at all.

Unfortunately, though, Derby's current concerning position in the Championship table may work against them in a potential Mehmeti deal, especially if a club like Birmingham look to reignite interest, too.

The 25-year-old wanted to prove he was Premier League quality back in August. If he's likely to do that elsewhere in January, a club near the top of the second tier would be an ideal place to showcase that.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

If he can get promoted for a second time in as many years, there wouldn't be much more a player could do to be given a chance in the top flight, especially if he contributes to a strong second half of the season at that club.

At Derby, he'd be tasked with helping a club stave off relegation and climb up the table, which may not be as impressive on his resume after this season.

So, if the Rams are to put themselves in the best position possible to attract Mehemti or other leading Championship players who are on the fringes of the Premier League, a good run of form between now and the new year will help them out massively.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2009. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2008. Joao Pedro Injury: Chelsea Forward Misses Brentford Defeat

Graeme Hanna is the site lead of Read Rangers and also writes about West Ham for Read West Ham. A Rangers season-ticket holder and freelance writer, he has previously written for Vital Rangers, Rangers Review, Football Ground Guide and Give Me Sport, and has a long association with the Follow Follow fanzine.

Joao Pedro missed Chelsea’s 3-0 Premier League defeat to Brentford with a knee problem, and the injury has since ruled him out of Brazil’s squad for the friendlies against Australia and India.

He was absent from Xabi Alonso’s confirmed lineups against Brentford, with Chelsea turning to other forward options instead.

Brazil’s coaching staff confirmed the withdrawal, pointing to the same knee issue that kept him out of the derby. Chelsea have not set a firm return date for Joao Pedro, leaving supporters to wait for further updates during the international break.

The Joao Pedro injury situation took a new turn when the Standard reported that he is seeing a specialist during the international break to speed up his recovery.

According to the Standard, the forward is using this pause in the calendar to get ahead of the problem rather than wait for Chelsea to resume domestic action.

Chelsea have not issued their own statement on the specialist visit, and the club’s official line on Joao Pedro’s fitness remains limited to his withdrawal from matchday duty.

Full detail on the reported treatment can be found in football.london’s reported injury update, which first carried the specialist claim alongside Xabi Alonso’s comments on the striker’s season.

Until Chelsea confirm otherwise, the Standard’s report stands as the clearest picture of how the club are handling the knee concern.

It suggests a measured approach, with recovery prioritised over rushing Joao Pedro back into contention for the next fixture.

Before the injury forced him out, Xabi Alonso had made his admiration for Joao Pedro clear. The Chelsea manager ranked the forward among the Premier League’s elite strikers, alongside Manchester City’s Erling Haaland.

“If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there, Haaland for sure is there.

“So I would rate him that way. He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, and to be a nominee for not just this month but more months. I am not surprised, but really happy with the kind of player that we have here with João.”

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Alonso must lean again on the depth built into his squad.

His approach to rotation, part of the squad management this season, faces another test while his in-form forward is unavailable.

#2007. Two days or two weeks – Michael Carrick future decision rolls into the international break

Manchester United will use the November international break to decide whether Michael Carrick stays on as head coach, after a three-game reprieve that delivered only one win.

According to The Guardian, Carrick came close to being sacked after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

Those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

Wilcox is now leading a review of Carrick’s position. He will consult Berrada before making a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who oversees the club’s sporting operations. Talks are expected to begin on Monday and continue through the break.

The league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

If he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

Carrick remains defiant. Speaking to Sky Sports News after the Villa draw, he admitted his side “haven’t won enough games” but insisted he expects to move forward.

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games, said Carrick after the late Villa draw.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”

If United do make a change, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reported to be Wilcox’s preferred candidate. Howe has been out of work since leaving St James’ Park during pre-season, after four and a half years in charge.

In the meantime, there are no plans to strengthen Carrick’s coaching staff.

For now, Carrick is expected to be in charge for United’s next match, against Liverpool. Whether three games were enough to convince the hierarchy should become clear before then.

The trip to Anfield could be do or die for the decorated former United midfielder.

He’s not likely to survive a heavy defeat at the home of the club’s fierce rivals, but a galvanising win would surely buy him time and goodwill.

That’s if he makes it through the next fortnight before then. A decision or indication could be two days or two weeks away.

The only certainty at Old Trafford is uncertainty.

#2006. Pep Guardiola Speaks Out as Man City Found Guilty of 114 Charges

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 financial charges, the Premier League has confirmed. The verdict follows an eight-week hearing that opened almost two years ago. It closes one of the most significant disciplinary cases in the competition’s history.

Former head coach Pep Guardiola has already broken his silence. Reaction to the Pep Guardiola Man City charges verdict is spreading fast across the division, with Chelsea among the clubs watching closely.

Guardiola joined Manchester City in 2016 and turned them into the dominant force in English football. He left his post earlier this summer, with the club having already worked through plans to replace Pep Guardiola at City.

His exit means he holds no formal role at the Etihad. Yet he moved quickly to make his loyalty clear once the ruling landed. According to the football.london report that first carried his statement, Guardiola posted directly to his supporters.

“I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman [Khaldoon Al Mubarak], Ferran [Soriano], the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.”

Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has confirmed that the club intends to appeal the verdict. The statement from Guardiola comes to City’s defence despite him leaving the role this summer. He is still viewed as the man who built this era of success, even though he no longer sits in the dugout at the Etihad.

The Pep Guardiola Man City charges case matters just as much to Chelsea as it does to Manchester City themselves. Chelsea, along with Arsenal and Tottenham, are among the Premier League clubs directly affected by the outcome. Every point City may have gained through breaches has a knock on effect further down the table.

Most top flight clubs including Chelsea are now pushing for City to face relegation as a consequence of the verdict. Some are reported to be weighing up legal action of their own. Guardiola has spoken about Chelsea before, including Guardiola’s previous comments on Chelsea. This latest statement fits a pattern of public backing for Manchester City, despite the criticism now directed at the club.

For Chelsea supporters, the case is not just about points on a table. It touches on the integrity of seasons they competed in directly. That is why so many rivals are refusing to let the matter rest with a guilty verdict alone.

Manchester City’s appeal process is now the next stage in a case that has already run for nearly two years. Ferran Soriano has made clear the club will contest the findings. No date has been confirmed for when that appeal will be heard.

Until then, no points deductions, penalties or changes to past titles have been confirmed by the Premier League. Chelsea and their rivals will be watching the appeal timeline just as closely as they watched the original hearing. The final outcome could still be a long way off.

#2005. Monaco summit adds unnecessary drama to Michael Carrick situation

Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington for Manchester United training as normal on Tuesday morning, while his bosses were preparing to decide his future in talks on the Mediterranean.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are flying to Monaco to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with the BBC reporting that the pair will recommend Carrick is sacked.The Guardian has indicated representatives of the Glazer family will also be involved.

The club insists the Monaco summit was pre-planned and is not solely about the head coach and while that may be true, it hardly matters.By allowing the meeting to become public knowledge, United have turned a straightforward football decision into unnecessary drama, compounding an already difficult situation.

What does is say about Man United in 2026 that a manager is given three games to secure his job, then left to train the squad during an international break while the executives are flying off to rule on his future? It’s farcical.

The latest chapter is another muddled process.Wilcox and Berrada met at Carrington the day after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October and agreed to give Carrick three more matches.A defeat at Chelsea, a win over Roma and a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa later, they appear to have reached the conclusion many expected a fortnight ago.

If the timeline holds, the decision will be made at Wednesday’s meeting, with an official announcement expected later in the week.United reportedly want to tell Carrick face to face, which means he could spend another day or two working under a cloud. In reality, it could be two days or two weeks.

The stakes could hardly be higher. United have won once in 10 league games, their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, and sit one point off the bottom in 18th place.

Should Carrick go, attention will turn quickly to his successor.ESPN reports that United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favoured candidate, while Eddie Howe has been named as Wilcox’s preferred choice. Antonio Conte has also been mentioned.

Carrick deserves better than this.Whatever the outcome, a club that wants to be taken seriously should not be settling its manager’s future in the full glare of the media while he is still out on the training pitch.

#2004. Alex Scott Chelsea Transfer Blocked as Bournemouth Eye January Stay

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bournemouth will block any Alex Scott Chelsea transfer in January. That is according to reports from the Daily Mail and BBC Sport. Both outlets say the Cherries want to keep their young midfielder as they fight to protect their Premier League status this season.

Chelsea have been linked with serious interest in the 22-year-old. Reports suggest the Blues have already tested Bournemouth’s resolve with a bid worth close to £64 million. Bournemouth have given no indication they are willing to negotiate. Scott, the reports say, simply is not for sale this winter.

Reports in the Daily Mail and on BBC Sport state that Bournemouth have no intention of sanctioning a sale this winter. The club’s hierarchy reportedly view Scott as central to their survival plan, wary of leaning on new signings mid-season rather than trusting the squad they already have.

A fee of around £64 million, first reported by Football London, is said to have been offered by Chelsea during recent discussions.

Scott joined Bournemouth from Bristol City in 2023. He has quickly become one of the most sought-after young midfielders in English football. Interest from a club the size of Chelsea shows how far his reputation has grown, though Bournemouth’s stance makes a January move increasingly unlikely.

Scott’s rise has been underlined by his first appearance for England. He came off the bench for a 20-minute cameo as Thomas Tuchel’s side beat Czechia 2-0 in the Nations League. The manager praised him afterwards.

“Alex Scott has maybe one of the best performances in midfield in the Premier League since the start with Bournemouth.”

“Individually he’s one of the outstanding midfielders so he clearly deserves to be with us.”

“He took another step into the right direction. Very impressive and happy that he is on that route. Now he plays in Europe for Bournemouth and deserves to be with us.”

That praise from their former manager will only increase Chelsea’s interest. Scott’s energy and composure suit the identity Xabi Alonso wants to build at Stamford Bridge. The Spaniard has already shown he is willing to rotate his squad, as seen in Xabi Alonso’s squad management decisions this season.

Chelsea travel to face Bournemouth in the Premier League soon. It is a fixture that will give Alonso a close look at a player repeatedly linked with his club. Build-up to that game is already underway, with team news arriving ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

The prospects of an Alex Scott Chelsea transfer happening in January now look slim. Supporters hoping for fresh competition in central midfield may need patience, with Chelsea more likely to revisit their interest when the summer window opens.

#2003. Celtic fans disgracefully boo during minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday: Referee ends tribute after just 13 SECONDS - even after warning from the PA announcer

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:28 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:51 EST, 9 November 2026

Celtic were forced to curtail plans to commemorate Remembrance Day after a section of their supporters booed during the planned minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The Bhoys hosted Kilmarnock in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday - with Liam Scales' goal proving the difference in a 1-0 win.

However, ahead of kick-off at Parkhead, the annual tribute to the armed forces and their families was overshadowed by some fans' loud jeers.

As the players from both teams gathered around the centre-circle, an announcement on the public address system said: 'We will have a minute's silence today on Remembrance Sunday to remember all victims of all conflicts. We remember, in particular, the men who served Celtic football club and lost their lives at wartime.'

The audible disdain resulted in referee John Beaton being forced to cut the silence after just 13 seconds.

The noise was so palpable that the Celtic TV broadcast turned down the volume to try and minimise its impact too.

The minute's silence ahead of Celtic versus Kilmarnock was cut short due to some fans booing

Celtic TV turned down the volume to try and minimise the jeers during the curtailed silence

Referee John Beaton (right) cut the minute's silence after 13 seconds as a result of the booing

Furthermore, the lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

Football clubs across the United Kingdom observe a minute's silence with their nearest home fixture around Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day - with the latter on November 11.

Many teams also wear poppies, something Kilmarnock wore on their strip, but Celtic didn't.

Some Celtic supporters refuse to partake in the tradition or actively take a stance against it, often citing the club’s Irish roots and linking it to the British Army‘s role in The Troubles.

Last season, in a quirk, Celtic hosted Kilmarnock on Remembrance Sunday too - with that minute's silence also cut short due to jeering. That time referee Don Robertson cut it short at 15 seconds.

As well as the booing in that match last term, some fans turned their back on the minute's silence and also made gestures.

Sunday's 1-0 win over Kilmarnock sees Celtic regain their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership.

It was under-pressure Martin O'Neill's side's first league win in their last three games.

Scales scored the only goal of the game on 26 minutes when he hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner.

Celtic fans show their displeasure during the minute's silence for Remembrance Day in 2025

Celtic - and Kasper Hogh in particular - otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

Celtic have 31 points from their opening 13 matches - four more than bitter rivals Rangers who sit second but have a game in hand.

Kilmarnock remain rooted to the bottom of the table with nine points from 13 games - two adrift of 11th-place Aberdeen who have played a match fewer.

Reggie Watson Chelsea news continues to build, according to football.london, with the 16-year-old further establishing himself as one of Xabi Alonso’s wildcard options in the first-team squad. Watson has been named in both of Chelsea’s senior squads for their Carabao Cup ties this season.

He was an unused substitute in the second-round win over Luton Town, then made his full Chelsea debut in the 6-3 win over Leeds United at Stamford Bridge. Watson played the first 45 minutes against Leeds, a reward for his progress since Alonso took charge at Chelsea over the summer.

#2000. “Quite simply disgusting”: Gary Neville tears into Manchester United over Carrick sacking

Graeme Hanna is the site lead of Read Rangers and also writes about West Ham for Read West Ham. A Rangers season-ticket holder and freelance writer, he has previously written for Vital Rangers, Rangers Review, Football Ground Guide and Give Me Sport, and has a long association with the Follow Follow fanzine.

Gary Neville has launched a furious attack on Manchester United’s leadership over the way the club handled Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

United confirmed on Thursday that Carrick had been sacked, four days after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games.

The club said it had reached the “extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary”.

Neville had already branded the process “classless” on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast before the announcement, pointing out that it was widely known Carrick was about to go while United were holding talks with potential replacements.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the decision was confirmed, the former United captain went even further.

“It’s just quite simply disgusting,” he said.

“That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.”

Neville took particular aim at the decision to hold the crucial meeting in Monaco, with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flying out to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick was still taking training at Carrington.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership,” he said.

It seems the only ones not to realise that are the trio above, but they aren’t stupid. How they explain it, or attempt to rationalise, it will be painful to listen to.

Neville also argued the club should have acted sooner. Looking back to the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in October, he said United “effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch” as he waved goodbye to supporters at full time, only for the board to hand him three more games.

He summed up the episode as “indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership”.

It’s more than an episode, it’s an omnishambles that reflects the dysfunctional state of MUFC in its current guise.

United are now expected to move quickly for Mauricio Pochettino. The United States head coach is reported to have reached an agreement in principle with the club, which is prepared to pay his release clause.

First, they will need to wait until the USMNT completes its CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

Yes. Man United to wait until an international break to appoint an international manager…

For Neville, though, the bigger problem lies above the dugout and no manager can be the scapegoat for that massive issue.

#1999. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.
